time_control.reference_time: Scenario-specific t=0; all hydrographs and boundary time series referenced to this origin.

simulation_horizon.extension_rule: Extend beyond 24 h when the flood-wave response, downstream boundary response, or relevant hydrograph tail has not adequately passed/stabilized within the primary domain.

timestep_sensitivity.purpose: Check whether the primary hydraulic outputs are sensitive to timestep restriction.

boundary_dependency.note: The downstream boundary condition is independent of the spatial domain length. The 28.29 km defines where the boundary is located; NORMAL_DEPTH defines the hydraulic condition imposed there.

mesh_dependency.important_rule: The actual stable computational timestep will be determined by CFL control after the hydraulic mesh and flow speeds are established.

quality_control: Do not interpret 30 s as a guaranteed stable timestep for every future mesh or scenario.
Confirm actual CFL-limited timesteps in the solver log.
Perform the 15 s maximum-timestep sensitivity on at least the primary provisional scenario.
Extend the simulation toward 48 h if the flood response has not sufficiently passed through the domain by 24 h.

deltares_dflow_fm.relevant_guidance: D-Flow FM uses CFL-based automatic timestep limitation; the manual advises a maximum Courant number of 0.7 or lower for the explicit advection scheme and describes initial and maximum timestep settings.

next_step: Update the hydraulic input register with the finalized domain, bed, roughness, downstream-boundary and time-control specifications, then perform the final Member-2 case QA.
